questions.q: What is the most common early mistake this lesson describes?
options: Using one workspace for everything, so an untested change can affect the same data real users depend on with nothing standing in between
Using too many separate workspaces for a small project
Writing KQL queries that are too simple
Deploying Activator rules before building any Eventstreams
questions.explain: One workspace means no separation between "I changed something" and "it's live."

questions.q: What mechanism from Lesson 15 moves item definitions between dev, test, and prod workspaces?
options: The Deployment Pipeline
The Monitoring Hub
Real-Time Dashboards
The Activator rule engine
questions.explain: This isn't a new concept — it's a deliberate policy for using an existing mechanism: nothing skips test.

questions.q: What should stay identical across dev, test, and prod, according to this lesson?
options: The KQL queries, Eventstream logic, and dashboard tiles themselves
The actual data in each environment
The permissions granted to each environment
The Fabric Capacity SKU used by each environment
questions.explain: That's the entire point of item-definition-only deployment — logic moves, data and permissions don't.

questions.q: Why shouldn't a dev or test environment point at real production data?
options: A bug in an untested query could write bad data into a table real dispatchers watch, or trigger a real alert to real people over a mistake
Production data is always too large to use anywhere else
There's no real risk involved — it's just a convention with no practical reason
Fabric technically prevents dev workspaces from ever accessing any data
questions.explain: Production-shaped test data — same schema, similar scale, safe to break — avoids this risk entirely.

options: Realistic test data with the same schema and rough scale as production, but not the real thing — safe to break
The actual live production data, copied into test for convenience
Randomly generated data with no relationship to the real schema
Data that only exists in the prod workspace
questions.explain: It lets test verify changes realistically without any risk of affecting real users or real alerts.
